newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown - no ceding of tax powers to EU.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown - no ceding of tax powers to EU.

text.p: British Opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Thursday a Labour government would not give up power over tax and public spending to the European Union.

"There should be no power to raise taxes removed from Britain to Europe, no power to decide on spending issues to be removed," Brown told a news conference. "We've made that absolutely clear over a long period."

Brown said Europe was a poisoned chalice for the ruling Conservatives, not Labour. "The question John Major has to answer....is how it is he is still being defied by his government ministers and he is still being defied by 245 (Conservative) candidates," Brown said.

He highlighted comments made by former Conservative minister John Redwood on BBC radio, earlier on Thursday. "The overwhelming majority of the Conservative Party...is instinctively against the abolition of the pound," Redwood said.

On Wednesday, Prime Minister John Major lit up the election campaign with an impassioned defence of his policy over Europe. He said two of his junior ministers had been reprimanded for abandoning the government's line in personal manifestos.
Later, in a hastily recorded television message, Major asked voters not to "tie his hands" in negotiations with European Union leaders by calling for EMU to be rejected now.
"How could this government, if it were re-elected, negotiate for Britain's interests in Europe in any way at all?" Brown asked.
Labour leader Tony Blair added that Conservative factions were in charge of the party's policy, not John Major.
